2608.11891.title: Benchmark-Based Comparative Assessment of Publicly Benchmarked Indian Foundation Models: A Capability and Evaluation-Maturity Framework
2608.11891.paper_summary: Governments increasingly fund indigenous foundation models to strengthen national AI capability, digital sovereignty, and multilingual computing. Assessing the progress of such national ecosystems is complicated by inconsistent benchmark reporting, proprietary evaluation methodologies, and rapidly evolving model releases. This paper presents a structured, benchmark-based comparative assessment of publicly benchmarked Indian foundation models against global frontier and comparable-scale models, across eight capability domains: general-purpose reasoning, coding and software engineering, agentic AI and computer use, cybersecurity, vision and image understanding, video and multimodal understanding, scientific research, and Indic language capability. Using only publicly reported benchmark results, we find that Indian models achieve strong scores on established benchmarks such as MMLU and MATH-500. However, these benchmarks are now widely regarded as saturated, and frontier developers no longer report them. Indian models participate far less frequently in newer, agentic, and domain-specialized evaluations. Benchmark participation is also highly uneven across Indian organizations. Among the models surveyed, Sarvam AI reports the broadest benchmark coverage by a substantial margin. We propose an exploratory four-dimension Benchmark Maturity Index (BMI), scoring each capability domain on standardization, participation, independent verification, and national coverage. We show that the BMI refines, and in some cases revises, the maturity judgments that a purely descriptive review would produce. We argue that many apparent capability gaps in the public record cannot be distinguished, on available evidence, from evaluation-ecosystem gaps. This has direct implications for how national AI programs should design monitoring and funding criteria.
2608.11891.paper_summary_zh: 政府越來越多地資助本土基礎模型，以增強國家的人工智慧能力、數位主權和多語言計算。評估這些國家生態系統的進展因基準報告不一致、專有評估方法和快速演變的模型發布而變得複雜。本文提供了一個結構化的、基於基準的比較評估，將公開基準的印度基礎模型與全球前沿和可比規模的模型進行比較，涵蓋八個能力領域：通用推理、編碼和軟體工程、自主人工智慧和計算機使用、網絡安全、視覺和圖像理解、視頻和多模態理解、科學研究以及印度語言能力。僅使用公開報告的基準結果，我們發現印度模型在MMLU和MATH-500等既定基準上取得了良好的分數。然而，這些基準現在被廣泛認為已經飽和，前沿開發者不再報告它們。印度模型在更新的、自主的和領域專門的評估中參與的頻率遠低於其他模型。基準參與在印度各組織之間也高度不均衡。在調查的模型中，Sarvam AI報告的基準覆蓋範圍以相當大的差距是最廣的。我們提出了一個探索性的四維基準成熟度指數（BMI），對每個能力領域在標準化、參與度、獨立驗證和國家覆蓋範圍上進行評分。我們展示了BMI如何精煉，並在某些情況下修訂純描述性評估所產生的成熟度判斷。我們認為，根據可用證據，公共記錄中許多明顯的能力差距無法與評估生態系統的差距區分開來。這對國家人工智慧計劃如何設計監測和資助標準具有直接的影響。
2608.11891.author: Avinash Agarwal et.al.
